transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I’m having a really hard time keeping my mind on one task long enough to finish it. Even when it’s important, like tracing a client’s network problem, I’ll look up and realize I’ve spent ten minutes rereading the same log entries over and over and still don’t really know what they say. It’s getting in the way of my work.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around a lot when you're supposed to be staying still?

Yes, a lot. Even when I’m supposed to just sit still and listen, I feel this kind of motor running under my skin. I’ll want to get up, check something, move on to the next problem—anything but just stay there calmly.

Do you often feel anxious or worried about things even when there isn't a clear reason for it, or does your restlessness usually come up more when you're trying to focus on something that's difficult or boring?

It’s more that it comes up when I’m supposed to sit still or stay with something. I don’t know that I’d call it worry exactly. It feels physical, like there’s a motor humming under my skin, and I need to stand up, check something, or move on to the next problem right away.
Do you experience this same restlessness and difficulty staying focused in other situations outside of work, like at home or when you're with friends or family?

Yes, it happens outside work too. At home, even things that are supposed to be relaxing don’t last long for me. If I’m reading a manual or trying to sit through a movie with my wife, after a few minutes I’m making little comments, checking my phone, or just getting up for no real reason. Even breathing exercises—I can’t seem to stay with them very long.
Looking back, did you start having trouble staying focused or feeling restless before you were 12 years old, or did these issues start more recently?

Oh, it definitely goes way back. My mother still jokes about my grade school report cards saying I was bright, but I wouldn’t stay in my seat, I’d blurt out answers, and I’d lose homework even when I’d actually done it. So no, it’s not something that just started recently.
